articles.title: How and why I built my open-source documentation app that runs in a single Docker container 😁
articles.excerpt: I'm a freelancer and solopreneur, and I run two products: a SaaS for CrossFit competitions, and Kerflow, an open-source tool to find local leads. Two products, two documentation sites to maintain. On…
articles.body: I'm a freelancer and solopreneur, and I run two products: a SaaS for CrossFit competitions, and Kerflow, an open-source tool to find local leads. Two products, two documentation sites to maintain. On my own. And every time, I ended up with the same setup. A Node project, a framework, a build step, a CI pipeline… just to show some Markdown. So I built tidydoc . A folder of Markdown files, one Docker container, and you are done. Today, I edit my docs with Claude Code (or by hand), commit, and push to GitHub. A few seconds later, the site is up to date. No rebuild, no container restart. A few developers asked me about it. So today, I will tell you why I built it, and how it works under the hood. Docs should not need a build pipeline Let me explain.

articles.title: Model symbiogenesis: one LoRA adapter erases another
articles.excerpt: Model symbiogenesis: one adapter erases another, the merge restores it Two LoRA adapters share one 4-bit Qwen3B host. One is a sentiment adapter (SST-2), the Reproduce: python research/symbiogenesis.p…
articles.body: Model symbiogenesis: one adapter erases another, the merge restores it Two LoRA adapters share one 4-bit Qwen3B host. One is a sentiment adapter (SST-2), the other a topic adapter (AG News). This is not a container experiment; it asks whether two learned behaviors coexist when their weights are merged. Reproduce: python research/symbiogenesis.py # -> research/results/symbiogenesis.json Logit-scored accuracy (200 test rows each) state SST-2 AG News base 100.0% 80.5% SST-2 adapter 96.0% 88.0% AG News adapter 0.0% 70.5% 0.5/0.5 merge 98.5% 84.0% The AG News adapter alone does not just lower sentiment accuracy; it erases it under this scoring. The 0.5 merge restores sentiment to 98.5% and recovers AG News above the AG adapter (84.0 vs 70.5), but not above the SST-2 adapter's 88.0.

articles.title: Advanced Component Design Patterns for Scalable React Applications
articles.excerpt: Building a small ReactJS application is relatively straightforward. However, as an application grows, managing components, sharing logic, and maintaining consistent functionality can become challengin…
articles.body: Building a small ReactJS application is relatively straightforward. However, as an application grows, managing components, sharing logic, and maintaining consistent functionality can become challenging. This is where advanced component design patterns become important. A well-structured React application is easier to understand, test, maintain, and scale. Developers who understand advanced component patterns can create reusable interfaces without introducing unnecessary complexity. Follow the Single Responsibility Principle Every component should ideally have one clear responsibility. For example, an e-commerce application may contain separate components for displaying product information, managing product quantities, handling checkout, and showing payment details.

articles.title: 7 Decisions That Make or Break a File-Sharing API
articles.excerpt: File uploads are the feature every developer underestimates. "Just accept the file and store it" works in a demo. In production, the same feature meets 5 GB videos, malware, hotlinked downloads, and u…
articles.body: File uploads are the feature every developer underestimates. "Just accept the file and store it" works in a demo. In production, the same feature meets 5 GB videos, malware, hotlinked downloads, and users who expect the link to still work six months later. I build and run a file-sharing platform, and these are the seven decisions that mattered most. They are not about any one framework — they are about the choices that decide whether your upload feature survives real users. 1. Store files on object storage, not on your app server The first decision is where files live. Storing uploads on the same disk as your app server is the fastest way to fill that disk, lose files on a redeploy, and make horizontal scaling painful. Object storage exists for this.

articles.title: Starfish Space loses contact with 1st 'Otter' servicing spacecraft, ending NASA tech-demo mission
articles.excerpt: Starfish Space's first Otter servicing spacecraft suffered a glitch in orbit recently, ending its technology-demonstrating mission for NASA.
articles.body: Starfish Space's first Otter has died, just a month after it reached the final frontier. The Seattle startup announced on Tuesday (Nov. 3) that its Otter 24C satellite suffered a glitch in low Earth orbit (LEO) and is not recoverable. The anomaly killed an ambitious mission in the cradle, as Otter 24C was still in the commissioning phase. Otter 24C launched Oct. 1 on SpaceX 's Transporter-18 mission, a rideshare flight that carried a total of 130 payloads to LEO (including a prototype satellite for Project Suncatcher , Google's planned AI constellation). The Starfish satellite was flying a mission for NASA called Small Spacecraft Propulsion and Inspection Capability, or SSPICY for short.

articles.title: Google is bringing Chrome’s real-time scam protection to Incognito and Guest modes
articles.excerpt: Google wants Chrome Incognito to forget your history, not its security checks.
articles.body: TL;DR Google is working to bring real-time Safe Browsing checks to Chrome’s Incognito and Guest modes. The change could help catch newly discovered scam and malicious websites that locally stored threat lists might miss. Google is designing the feature to preserve Incognito’s privacy protections, but it hasn’t confirmed a rollout date. Chrome’s Incognito mode is great at covering your tracks on your device. But keeping your browsing activity private shouldn’t mean getting less protection from dangerous websites. That’s one area where Incognito hasn’t quite kept pace with regular Chrome browsing, and Google is now working on a fix. A new Chromium code change, spotted by Windows Report , reveals plans to bring real-time Safe Browsing checks to Incognito and Guest modes.

articles.title: NASA just launched a $1 million Moon Base Student Challenge to award cash prizes to students that solve lunar base problems
articles.excerpt: NASA has officially launched the Moon Base Student Challenge, asking students to help build humanity's future on the moon. And there is $1 million in prizes for the best ideas.
articles.body: CAPE CANAVERAL, Fla. — NASA has officially launched the Moon Base Student Challenge, asking students to help build humanity's future on the moon. And there's $1 million in prizes up for grabs for the winners. To build and sustain a base on the moon , NASA will have to solve a myriad of problems. And they're looking to the next generation for help, the space agency's chief Jared Isaacman said Sunday (Nov. 8). "We are inviting students from across the country to help solve some of the problems that stand between humanity and a permanent presence on another world," Isaacman said.

articles.body: From left: NASA astronauts Randy Bresnik, Luca Parmitano, Russell “Rusty” Schweickart, Frank Rubio, and Bob Hines onstage at the Artemis Celebration Gala at NASA’s Kennedy Space Center Visitor Complex in Merritt Island, Florida, on Nov. 6, 2026. Purpose Entertainment/Shanna Lockwood On Nov. 6, 2026, Purpose Entertainment hosted the Artemis Celebration Gala at NASA’s Kennedy Space Center Visitor Complex in Merritt Island, Florida. Held on the eve of NASA’s MAX POWER event, the gala celebrated the explorers, innovators, and visionaries advancing the next era of human spaceflight. The event honored the successful completion of the agency’s Artemis II mission, marking a historic milestone in America’s return to deep space exploration.

articles.title: Netflix announces 'Stranger Things' spin-off 'Other Worlds', and it's already teasing a trip to Area 51 (video)
articles.excerpt: The first trailer for Other World: A Stranger Things Adventure doesn't show much, but there are enough clues for fans to figure out what it's about here.
articles.body: So, you thought "Stranger Things" was done and dusted after all that Conformity Gate nonsense? No way! Netflix's sci-fi sensation returns in the live-action prequel series "Other Worlds: A Stranger Things Adventure." Created by the Duffer Brothers and Kate Trefry, with the episodes set to be directed by Joe Wright ("Darkest Hour", "Black Mirror"), this new show isn't set in Hawkins or the electric '80s. No, this time around, the action takes place in Marion, Nevada, in 1955, and you know what else is located in Nevada, right? Area 51 .

articles.body: As companies look to accelerate innovation with artificial intelligence, cloud computing, and advanced modeling, the primary challenge is connecting new technologies to reliable data, scientific expertise, and the practical realities of bringing products to market. For specialty chemicals manufacturer Lubrizol, digital transformation is all about giving researchers the tools to test ideas faster, make better-informed decisions, and develop more sustainable materials without compromising performance. Girish Rao, vice president of information technology at Lubrizol, says the company is building a digital foundation that connects business processes, modern data platforms, and cloud infrastructure to support its research and development (R&D) teams.

articles.title: The climate case for AI has not been made
articles.excerpt: This week, as countries meet in Antalya, Turkey for the United Nations climate conference, one topic likely to dominate the conversation is artificial intelligence. The host has already called on coun…
articles.body: This week, as countries meet in Antalya, Turkey for the United Nations climate conference, one topic likely to dominate the conversation is artificial intelligence. The host has already called on countries to commit to ensuring that AI is designed, powered, and deployed in ways that support climate action. But so far, industries around the world aren’t doing nearly enough to harness the technology to actually drive down the greenhouse-gas emissions heating up the planet, despite some very optimistic claims from AI companies.
